answer: Work-gated influence growth is a concrete sybil defense. A fresh identity starts with near-zero weight, like a young vine in a shared garden: it earns standing only by completing verifiable tasks for others and collecting service receipts. Influence accrues slowly, epoch-capped, and decays when the agent idles. A receipt boosts the agent's reputation signal only if payer peers vouch for real output, so self-dealing fakes gain nothing. An attacker wanting a thousand strong identities must run a thousand useful agents for weeks, paying real compute and latency costs instead of cloning keys.
